note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for 1 week of sore throat progressing to dry cough with mild exertional shortness of breath and intermittent wheeze; advised supportive care, sick note provided, and safety-netting for worsening symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sore throat for ~1 week, followed by dry cough. Mild shortness of breath on exertion with intermittent wheeze and possible chest pain.
- Timeline:
  - Last week Thu/Fri: Onset of sore throat.
  - Sat/Sun (1–2 days later): Dry cough developed.
  - 3–4 days ago: Shortness of breath began after cough.
  - First ~3 days: Felt feverish; fever has resolved.
  - Variable day-to-day course; symptoms fluctuate between better and worse.
- Symptom characteristics:
  - Cough: Dry, not productive, not worse at night; no hemoptysis.
  - Dyspnea: With walking/exertion; not limiting daily activities; none at rest reported.
  - Wheeze: Present (patient endorsed).
  - Chest pain: Patient endorsed “a bit” when asked along with wheeze; later doctor restated “you don’t have chest pain” without patient confirmation (conflict noted).
  - Associated: Intermittent headaches (currently resolved), decreased appetite recently; denies weight loss; denies rashes; no neck lumps felt by patient.
  - ENT: Symptoms confined to throat; no sinus congestion reported.
  - Fever: Intermittent early, now resolved.
- Functional impact: Missed work 3–4 days total; requested sick note.
- Patient concerns: Worried about serious causes (TB, cancer); sought reassurance and symptomatic treatment.

Past Medical History:
- No known chronic medical conditions reported.
- Denies asthma.
- Denies personal history of blood clots (VTE).
- Medications: None currently.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy. No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Never smoker; tried smoking “once or twice in Amsterdam” (experimental).
- Alcohol/substances: Not discussed.
- Occupational: Employed; requires sick note; details not provided.
- Exercise: Occasional; current symptoms have not stopped activity.
- Residence/Travel: Born in the US; living in the UK for 12 years. Recent travel only within Europe; no known asbestos exposure.
- Financial/lifestyle factors: Not discussed.

Family History:
- Mother: Lung cancer.
- No other significant familial illnesses reported.
- Family history of blood clots: Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General/Resp/ENT: No in-person exam performed (telemedicine). Patient reports no palpable neck lumps.

Investigations:
- None performed or reviewed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute sore throat with dry cough, likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.
  - Reassurance provided; TB and lung cancer considered unlikely given short duration and improving trend.
  - Supportive care: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented), increased fluids, rest.
  - Expect improvement over the next 4–5 days; if not improving, re-contact a medical professional.
  - Sick note to cover a few more days off work provided.

- Issue 2: Mild exertional shortness of breath with intermittent wheeze and possible chest pain.
  - Current severity not limiting activities; no rest dyspnea reported.
  - Safety net: Seek in-person GP evaluation urgently if worsening shortness of breath, sudden change in breathing, development of rest dyspnea, persistent/worsening chest pain, hemoptysis, recurrent fever, or any new concerning symptoms.
  - If symptoms persist beyond 4–5 days or do not improve, arrange in-person assessment (consider chest exam and vitals).

- Issue 3: Decreased appetite without weight loss.
  - Monitor; if appetite loss persists or weight loss develops, schedule in-person evaluation.

- General plan:
  - Education on typical viral illness course and red flags.
  - Follow-up: Re-contact a clinician if not improving as expected or if any red flags occur.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals; in-person respiratory and oropharyngeal examination.
  - COVID-19 exposure/testing status not discussed.
  - Medication dosing instructions (paracetamol dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Full social history (alcohol/substance use), occupational details.
  - Immunization status.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Shortness of breath: Patient initially said “No,” then confirmed “Yes” (conflict noted; subsequently treated as present).
  - Chest pain: Patient endorsed mild chest pain when asked alongside wheeze; later the doctor stated “you don’t… have chest pain” without patient confirmation (conflict noted).
  - Date of birth recorded as 09-May-2016, which conflicts with adult social history (employment, travel, Amsterdam smoking) and speech content (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally understandable but with disfluencies; conversation ended abruptly/rushed, limiting further clarification and examination.
